insulin_sensitivity.text: Insulin sensitivity reflects how strongly tissues respond to insulin signaling. Lower values require more insulin to produce similar glucose lowering.

beta_cell_function.text: Beta-cell function represents the pancreas' ability to secrete insulin over time. Declining function weakens peak response and slows glucose recovery.

provenance.note: Educational definition used in chart callouts.

hepatic_glucose_output.text: Hepatic glucose output is liver-derived glucose entering circulation. If suppression is weak, fasting and pre-meal glucose remain elevated.

peripheral_uptake.text: Peripheral uptake approximates glucose removal by muscle and other tissues. More activity and stronger signaling increase this pathway.

what_this_graph_shows.normal: This graph shows how meal carbohydrate load raises glucose, how insulin responds, and how quickly glucose returns toward baseline. Use it to compare peak height, response timing, and recovery slope.
what_this_graph_shows.resistance: This graph shows the mismatch between rising glucose and less effective insulin action when resistance increases. Watch for a higher peak and slower return toward baseline.
what_this_graph_shows.beta: This graph shows how declining beta-cell capacity weakens insulin response and lengthens glucose recovery. Compare peak timing and whether baseline is regained within the window.
what_this_graph_shows.complications: This graph shows persistent glycemic burden over time, which feeds downstream risk scores. Use it as the signal source behind organ risk trajectories.

why_glucose_changed_template.text: Glucose changed because carbohydrate load was {carbs_g}g, activity was {activity_min} min, insulin sensitivity was {insulin_sensitivity_pct}%, and beta-cell function was {beta_cell_function_pct}%. Higher carbs raises the peak, while stronger uptake and insulin response lower the peak and shorten recovery.
